preview.tournamentOverview: Baycurrent Classic is played at Yokohama Country Club, a course that places a premium on ball-striking and off-the-tee accuracy. The layout rewards players who can keep the ball in play off the tee and convert opportunities into birdies while avoiding big numbers. This event matters because it offers a strong field and a unique test that separates elite ball-strikers from the field.
preview.modelExplainer: Our model weights SG Off-the-Tee at 1% and SG Total at 3%, making driving distance and accuracy the dominant factors this week. SG Approach 1%) and SG Putting 4%) follow, while SG Around-the-Green 0%) and ancillary stats like Bogey Avoidance 0%) and Birdie/Bogey Ratio 0%) round out the profile.
preview.pickApproach: We tier our bets by combining tournamentRank and powerRank, prioritizing golfers who rank inside the top 10 in both metrics. Secondary bets target players with strong SG OTT and SG APP marks who may be slightly lower in the overall rankings but still project well at Yokohama. We avoid overexposure to putting-heavy profiles given the lower weight on SG Putting this week.

article.title: Baycurrent Classic Model Targets: Lee, Bridgeman, Morikawa Lead Yokohama Fit
article.dek: Tournament model ranks Min Woo Lee #1, Jacob Bridgeman #2, and Collin Morikawa #3 for the 72-player field at Yokohama Country Club.
article.introduction: The Baycurrent Classic model weights SG OTT at 1% and SG Total at 3%, producing a top-20 list led by Min Woo Lee 693 SG Total, rank #1) and Jacob Bridgeman 933 SG Total, rank #2). Collin Morikawa sits third with 53 SG Total and 066 SG APP. All three players share the same post-Open research profile: DID_NOT_PLAY at the Open, skipped the Scottish Open, and zero tracked rounds in the major-swing workload window.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: The 72-player Baycurrent Classic at Yokohama Country Club carries course weights of SG OTT 1%, SG Total 3%, and SG PUTT 4%. The model ranks 20 players by weighted strokes-gained, with the top three separated by 163 strokes from Lee 693) to Morikawa 53).

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: Yokohama's emphasis on SG OTT 1%) and SG APP 1%) favors players with strong tee-to-green numbers. Lee posts 675 SG OTT and 266 SG APP; Bridgeman shows 245 SG OTT and 501 SG APP; Morikawa leads the trio with 542 SG OTT and 066 SG APP.

sections.heading: Recent Form
sections.body: Lee enters with power rank #8 and 693 SG Total. Bridgeman arrives at power rank #4 and 933 SG Total. Morikawa sits at power rank #9 and 53 SG Total. All three rank inside the model's top 10.

sections.heading: Post-Open Workload
sections.body: Each of the three targets recorded NO_TRACKED_ROUNDS in the major-swing workload window. Lee, Bridgeman, and Morikawa all carry the DID_NOT_PLAY flag for the Open and skipped the Scottish Open.

sections.heading: FedExCup Motivation
sections.body: Lee sits SAFE_TOP_50 at rank #21, Bridgeman at rank #13, and Morikawa at rank #7. All three hold buffer inside the top 50 with no immediate pressure to climb.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: The shared profile—Skipped the Scottish Open + top-10 model rank—applies to Lee (model rank #1), Bridgeman (model rank #2), and Morikawa (model rank #3).

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: Min Woo Lee (model rank #1, power rank #8) and Jacob Bridgeman (model rank #2, power rank #4) are the two outright targets. Both carry 693-plus SG Total marks and identical research flags.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: Lee, Bridgeman, and Collin Morikawa (model rank #3, 066 SG APP) form the top-10 card. Morikawa's approach game supplies the strongest SG APP figure among the three.

sections.heading: Top-20 Targets
sections.body: The same trio—Lee, Bridgeman, Morikawa—extends to top-20 cards. Their combined SG PUTT average of 563 aligns with the course's 4% weight on putting.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are not available in this pipeline; the article does not make weather- or tee-time-specific claims.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Tier 1 (model-supported): Min Woo Lee, Jacob Bridgeman. Tier 2 (model-supported): Collin Morikawa.

article.conclusion: Tier 1 model-supported outright and top-5 plays: Min Woo Lee and Jacob Bridgeman. Tier 2 top-10/top-20 addition: Collin Morikawa. All three share identical research flags and rank inside the model's top three.

keyTakeaways.text: Min Woo Lee tops the model at rank #1 with 1.693 SG Total and power rank #8, backed by 0.675 SG OTT and 0.457 SG PUTT.
Jacob Bridgeman ranks #2 with 1.933 SG Total and power rank #4, driven by 1.339 SG PUTT and 0.501 SG APP.
Collin Morikawa ranks #3 with 1.53 SG Total and 1.066 SG APP, the strongest approach figure in the top 20.
All three targets share identical research flags: DID_NOT_PLAY at the Open, skipped Scottish Open, and NO_TRACKED_ROUNDS in the major-swing workload window.
Course weights favor SG OTT (34.1%) and SG PUTT (16.4%), aligning with the top three players' combined 1.86 SG OTT and 1.69 SG PUTT averages.
